newsitem.title: EGYPT: Unrest will hit Middle East tourism, minister says.
newsitem.headline: Unrest will hit Middle East tourism, minister says.

text.p: Unrest in the Middle East will have severe effects on tourism, especially on tours which take in more than one country, Egyptian Tourism Minister Mamdouh el-Beltagi said in an interview published on Wednesday.
Beltagi also said that Egyptian private-sector travel agencies boycotted a tourism meeting in Tunisia last week in protest at Israeli policies.
"The whole region is going to suffer a strong decline in the number of tourists, not only Israel," the minister told the French-language weekly al-Ahram Hebdo.

"If the situation doesn't calm down, the system of packages between us, Israel and Jordan will suffer direct repercussions. I have recently received information from travel agencies that German and Italian groups have cancelled their reservations on tours of Egypt, Jordan and Israel," he said.
The West Bank and Gaza saw the worst violence in years last month after Israel opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem. More than 70 people were killed in the clashes.
Beltagi said Egyptian businessmen declined to attend the meeting in Tunisia last week of the executive council of the Middle East-Mediterranean Travel and Tourism Association.

"It was in solidarity with the Palestinian delegation, against the Israeli attacks in Jerusalem and Ramallah," he said. "The absence of Egypt led to the cancellation of the meeting, because all members have to be present."
The minister said two tourism cooperation projects were in doubt because of uncertainty about Middle East peace.
One is a "tourism university" to train Arab and Israeli students together and the other is a project to remove the barriers to the free movement of tourists in the region.
"I believe implementing these projects will be suspended until the regional situation becomes stable," he said.
